config.title: Custom property fallbacks

intro.title: Custom property fallbacks
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that uses CSS custom properties (variables) to style elements, and you will learn how to provide backup values, called fallbacks, in case a custom property is not defined. You will understand the core concept of graceful degradation in CSS by using the var() function with a second argument as a fallback value. The main technologies involved are CSS custom properties and the var() function. This will help you create more robust and maintainable stylesheets that work even when variables are missing.
intro.usecase: Custom property fallbacks are essential in professional CSS for building resilient design systems. In dashboard applications, fallbacks ensure charts and data visualizations maintain consistent colors even when theme variables are missing. Form components use fallbacks to guarantee accessible contrast ratios when custom brand colors aren't defined. This pattern prevents UI breakage in complex applications like admin panels or e-commerce filters where multiple themes and user preferences interact.

objectives: Implement custom properties with fallback values in CSS declarations
Apply multiple fallback values using the var() function syntax
Construct CSS rules that gracefully degrade when custom properties are undefined
Configure component styles with layered fallback strategies
Update existing CSS code to incorporate custom property fallbacks
Manipulate fallback values to create responsive design variations
Integrate custom property fallbacks with other CSS features like media queries

steps.title: Create a CSS file and define a custom property with a fallback value
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and define a custom property called --primary-color with a fallback value of blue using the var() function syntax.
steps.hint: Start by declaring a CSS custom property (CSS variable) with a fallback value. The syntax is: var(--variable-name, fallback-value).
steps.seedCode: /* Define your custom property with fallback here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS custom property named --primary-color is defined with a fallback value of blue using the var() function.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a custom property declaration using var(--primary-color, blue).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct syntax: var(--primary-color, blue).
steps.feedbackWrong: define a custom property called --primary-color with a fallback value of blue using var().

steps.title: Apply the custom property to an element
steps.instruction: Create a div element and apply the --primary-color custom property to its color property using the var() function with the fallback value.
steps.hint: Use the var() function to reference your custom property. The syntax is: color: var(--primary-color, fallback-value);
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element will be styled with the custom property value for its text color, using the fallback if the custom property is not defined.
successCriteria: The code includes a div selector with color property set using var(--primary-color, blue).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the var() function with both the custom property name and fallback value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your syntax. You need to use var(--primary-color, blue) to apply the custom property with its fallback.

steps.title: Test the fallback behavior by omitting the custom property definition
steps.instruction: Comment out the --primary-color custom property definition in the :root selector to see the fallback value (blue) take effect.
steps.hint: Add /* and */ around the --primary-color line to comment it out, or simply delete the line.
steps.expectedOutcome: The --primary-color custom property definition is commented out or removed, leaving only the fallback value in the var() function to be used.
successCriteria: The --primary-color line inside :root is commented out or removed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the --primary-color line inside the :root selector is fully commented out or removed.
steps.feedbackWrong: The --primary-color definition is still active. Comment it out or delete it to test the fallback behavior.

steps.title: Define multiple custom properties with different fallback values
steps.instruction: In the :root selector, add two new custom properties: --secondary-color with a fallback value of red, and --font-size with a fallback value of 16px.
steps.hint: Add the properties directly inside the existing :root block, each on its own line. Remember to use the var() function syntax with the fallback value after a comma.
steps.expectedOutcome: The :root selector will contain three custom properties, each with their own fallback values.
successCriteria: Two new custom properties are defined in the :root selector: --secondary-color with fallback red and --font-size with fallback 16px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some custom properties, but check that you have exactly two new ones: --secondary-color with fallback red and --font-size with fallback 16px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding two specific custom properties with fallback values in the :root selector. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Apply multiple custom properties to different elements
steps.instruction: Create two new div elements after the existing one. Apply the --secondary-color custom property to the background-color of the first new div, and the --font-size custom property to the font-size of the second new div.
steps.hint: Add two new div selectors. Use the var() function with the custom property names and their fallback values for the background-color and font-size properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two new div elements are added with custom properties applied to different CSS properties.
successCriteria: Two new div selectors are created with background-color and font-size properties using var() with the correct custom property names.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the div elements, but make sure to use var() with the correct custom property names for background-color and font-size.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create two new div elements and apply the custom properties to their respective CSS properties.

steps.title: Nest custom property usage with fallbacks
steps.instruction: Define a new custom property named --accent-color inside the :root selector. Set its value to var(--secondary-color, orange) to demonstrate nested fallback usage.
steps.hint: Add a new line after the existing custom properties in the :root selector. Use the syntax --accent-color: var(--secondary-color, orange);
steps.expectedOutcome: The :root selector will contain a new custom property --accent-color that references --secondary-color with orange as a fallback value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added --accent-color inside the :root selector with the exact value var(--secondary-color, orange).
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires defining a new custom property --accent-color with the value var(--secondary-color, orange) inside the :root selector.

steps.title: Apply the nested custom property
steps.instruction: Apply the --accent-color custom property to the border-color of the second div element.
steps.hint: Add a border-color property to the .box2 selector and set its value to var(--accent-color, orange).
steps.expectedOutcome: The second div element will have a border color defined by the --accent-color custom property, with orange as the fallback.
successCriteria: The .box2 selector includes a border-color property set to var(--accent-color, orange).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added border-color: var(--accent-color, orange); to the .box2 selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match the expected action. Please add border-color: var(--accent-color, orange); to the .box2 selector.

steps.title: Test the nested fallback chain
steps.instruction: Comment out the --secondary-color definition in the :root rule to observe how the fallback chain resolves to orange for --accent-color.
steps.hint: Add /* and */ around the --secondary-color line to comment it out, leaving the --font-size definition intact.
steps.expectedOutcome: The --secondary-color definition is commented out, making it undefined. This will cause the nested custom property --accent-color (which depends on --secondary-color) to fall back to orange.
successCriteria: The --secondary-color line in the :root rule is commented out with CSS comment syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the --secondary-color line needs to be fully commented out using /* and */.
steps.feedbackWrong: The --secondary-color definition should be commented out to test the fallback chain. Use CSS comment syntax: /* --secondary-color: green; */

steps.title: Create a custom property with multiple fallback values
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .button element that uses the var() function with multiple fallback values: set background-color to var(--custom-bg, var(--fallback-bg, gray)).
steps.hint: The var() function can accept multiple fallback values separated by commas. The syntax is var(--property, fallback1, fallback2).
steps.expectedOutcome: A .button CSS rule is added with background-color using var(--custom-bg, var(--fallback-bg, gray)) to demonstrate multiple fallback levels.
successCriteria: The .button rule exists and uses var() with multiple fallback values for background-color.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your .button rule uses var() with exactly the specified fallback chain: var(--custom-bg, var(--fallback-bg, gray)).
steps.feedbackWrong: The .button rule is missing or doesn't use the correct var() syntax with multiple fallback values. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Apply and test the multi-level fallback
steps.instruction: Create a button element and apply the --button-bg custom property to its background-color.
steps.hint: Define a .button class with background-color using var(--button-bg, fallback-chain).
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element styled with a custom property that uses a multi-level fallback chain.
successCriteria: The .button rule is defined with background-color using var(--button-bg, var(--primary-color, red)).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the .button rule uses var(--button-bg, var(--primary-color, red)) for background-color.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction. You need to create a .button rule with background-color using the custom property fallback chain.
